decisions.executionNote: Approach the green-handled crimper in the right workspace with small right-arm movements; keep left arm stationary and gripper open while checking geometry.
Previous approach was rejected without movement; halve the initial increments to preserve IK continuity.
Raise the wrist slightly and gradually pitch the right gripper downward for an overhead grasp; target remains the green-handled tool just ahead of the right fingers.
Continue gradual downward pitch and advance above the crimper, preserving clearance while the wrist view resolves the green handles.
Move the right wrist above the handle region while completing most of the downward approach orientation; maintain open jaws and height.
Finish pitching the right gripper vertically downward above the crimper; maintain a pregrasp clearance before aligning jaw direction.
Rotate the downward-facing right jaws gradually so they can close across, rather than along, the crimper handles.
Continue jaw alignment while descending only two centimeters toward the handle pregrasp; retain clearance and inspect RGB.
Complete near-perpendicular jaw alignment across the green handles while lowering cautiously toward contact height.
Use the wrist view to center the open jaws slightly farther forward across the handles and descend two centimeters cautiously.
At apparent handle contact height, hold the wrist steady and close the right gripper around the green-handled crimper; retention is not yet confirmed.
Keep the right gripper commanded closed and make a slow four-centimeter test lift, checking that the crimper follows rather than relying on gripper state.
The handles remain between the jaws in RGB during the test lift. Continue lifting vertically with the gripper closed toward the requested ten-centimeter clearance.
The crimper is visibly following the right gripper but its head hangs below the handles. Lift another five centimeters to provide clear ten-centimeter object clearance.
The crimper remains in the jaws but has tilted downward. Continue a slower four-centimeter vertical lift with the gripper closed, monitoring retention and clearance.
RGB suggests the crimper has slipped from the jaws. Open and lower cautiously to prepare a more secure grasp closer to the hinge after it settles.
The crimper has settled on the table in a new diagonal orientation. Approach its hinge with open jaws and rotate to close across its narrower neck rather than the handle tips.
Refine alignment over the hinge and lower in small increments, keeping the open fingers clear of the neighboring ball.
Visually center the hinge between the right fingers, moving slightly left and back while descending four centimeters toward a deeper, balanced grasp.
The narrow crimper neck is now centered between the jaws in the wrist view. Lower only 1.5 cm to seat the fingers before closing.
Close the right fingers around the centered hinge/handle-root region and pause briefly to establish a less tip-biased grasp.
Test the new hinge-centered grasp with a slow four-centimeter vertical lift, keeping the right gripper commanded fully closed.
The hinge-centered grasp appears stable in RGB. Continue lifting straight upward another six centimeters while maintaining the closed gripper.
The crimper remains stable relative to the fingers. Lift five more centimeters to exceed ten centimeters with clearance, without changing grasp orientation.
